note: Rio Grande NF, ~9,600 ft, SW of South Fork: US-160 west 13.5 mi, then 2.7 mi up gravel FR 390 (single-lane with turnouts). The loop sits in a spruce grove by a meadow, opened up by beetle-kill removal, with views of Fox Mountain. The two stocked Tucker Ponds (~10 acres each) are across the road from the entrance, not in the campground. --Claude
summary: FS page: confirmed 15 sites, max spur 40 ft (not all fit), FCFS only, 14-day limit, vault toilets, potable water, $26 (double $52); added season Memorial Day - Labor Day weekends, the 50% Senior/Access discount, concessionaire trash. Note cleaned of field facts. FR 390 flood closure is ~4 mi beyond the campground. Not waterfront kept.
flags: Phone: none stored. Divide Ranger District, Del Norte, (719) 657-3321 (FS page, Office Contact Information). Suggest 719-657-3321.

Access road, FS wording in full: 'From South Fork, CO: Take Hwy 160 west (toward Pagosa Springs) 13.5 miles to campground sign. Turn left at sign onto Rd. 390 (gravel) and go 2.7 miles to another campground sign. Turn right at sign into campground. NOTE: Forest Rd. 390 is single-lane with turnouts.' No 4WD, high-clearance or RV wording. The FS road atlas has FR 390 mileposts 0-8.75 as maintenance level 3 'suitable for passenger cars', crushed aggregate; the campground is at about MP 2.8.

October 2026 flooding: Rio Grande NF conditions page (updated October 28, 2026) lists 'FSR 390 from FSR 380 to the intersection with FSR 388 - impassable and closed to traffic - Divide Ranger District'. By the FS road atlas that is FR 390 from its east end (MP 8.75, the FR 380 junction) back to the FR 388 (Bonito) junction at about MP 6.9, roughly 4 miles beyond the campground, which is at about MP 2.8 from US-160. The approach from US-160 is not in the closed stretch. No closure of the campground itself (its season ended Labor Day weekend).
Operator: a concessionaire (FS: 'Concessionaire operations for 2026 season will begin May 22nd'; trash 'provided by the concessionaire'), not named. Ownership federal stands.
Pin 37.49437,-106.76075 equals the FS coordinates, at the campground entrance off FR 390. OK.

Waterfront 'not waterfront' kept (checked both ways): on NAIP the loop lies west of FR 390 behind a dense conifer band; the nearer (south) pond's west shore is ~70-80 m from the loop's east side, across the road and the trees. No apron and no open view, and the FS places the ponds 'across the road from the entrance to the campground'. Pass Creek is reached 'by hiking west of the campground'.
